findings.description: The page states 'QMA is closed under complement: coQMA = QMA. This uses the quantum error reduction technique (applying the swap test).' This is wrong on two counts. findings.description: [schema-cleanup audit 2026-08-21, medium] ## Ring-SIS: "the matrix is the negacyclic convolution matrix of a random $a \getsr R_q$, and a Ring-SIS solution is a short polynomial $z \in R$ with $a \cdot z = 0$ in $R_q$". The standard Ring-SIS (as in LM06) samples $m$ ring elements $a_1,\dots,a_m$ and asks for short $z_1,\dots,z_m$ with $\sum_i a_i z_i = 0$; the single-element version stated here is a different (degenerate) problem. Report only.

findings.description: [schema-cleanup audit 2026-08-21, medium] ### Collision-resistant hash functions: "restricted to inputs $\mathbf{z} \in \{0, \ldots, \lfloor \beta/2 \rfloor\}^m$ ... yields $\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{z}') = \mathbf{0} \pmod q$ with $\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{z}'\| \leq \beta$". The bound holds only in the $\ell_\infty$ norm; in $\ell_2$ (the norm the SIS game presumably uses, unspecified on the page) the difference can have norm up to $(\beta/2)\sqrt{m}$. The page never states which norm $\|\cdot\|$ denotes. Report only.
